# Read of unit U2, goal the-box-clock-counts-only-the-goals-own-work

Subject: worktree diff /Users/wido/.metasystem/unit/20261109t053112-8cf47bc210/round-1/worktree.diff
(SHA-256 5cad06a7dc249fd0e42baef06f5158f6f8a0c4cd9373dc676ce598ffe89b3f1e, verified; identical to the
launch read.diff) against base 0cb01e37487040112417b5e523405fe51f17c389, judged against the build brief
/Users/wido/.metasystem/unit/.inputs/be2de2835e579735c79326c71bec4929/build-brief.md.

## Result

AGREE. No material findings.

## Checklist 1: the diff against the brief

Every production item of the brief is present and correct:

- Item 1 (budget_provider.go): `clockDependency.id`; `providerWaits` sets `id: record.ID`. Nothing else in
  providerWaits changed; its early local-only return and its normal return both return every dependency.
- Item 2 (budget.go job loop): the environment set is filled right after `operations[operationID] = logicalPath`,
  before the `unitUnaccounted` and later `continue`s, for `unitRun != ""`, `TerminalStatus(status)` and
  `unitEnvironment == true` (S2). The reservation jobId is the launch id, so the provider-wait dependency's id joins.
- Item 3 (governed loop): after the excludeRunID/goal skip and the Governed/GoalRevision refusals, a
  non-terminal run with a readable `startedAt` appends `{at, "local", now, executed}` to `dependencies` (S1).
  An unreadable one records the fallback reason. Charge logic is unchanged.
- Item 4 (budget_own_work.go): executed, non-environment work; zero `at` falls back naming the job and
  runtime; zero `until` counts to now; environment intervals cut seat occupancy only (a build during a cut
  still counts, S5). Seat reader: skips non-.json files and other goals; missing dir means no seats; end =
  terminal launch FinishedAt, else reapedAt, else now (S3); not-found launch is not a failure. Every S4 failure
  falls back. The result is clipped to [start, now] as `Paused(W ∪ P) − Paused(P)` on fresh slices, never below 0.
  Seats never reach cutPersonWork, personWaits, providerWaits or wait.observe (D4 third rule).
- Item 5 (wiring): the legacy path is untouched and computed first (S7). The own-work call sits after
  `projection.Elapsed = max(...)`, inside the `!working && !budgetStartedAt.IsZero()` block, only under
  authorityLens, with `deps` and `slices.Clone(spans)`. On fallback it sets ElapsedLegacy and appends one problem
  line ("elapsed counts wall time less pauses: " + reason). `finishBudgetProjection` runs after the replacement,
  so mutation (l) holds.
- Item 6: `ElapsedLegacy bool json:"-"`.
- Item 7: `elapsedOverrunMin` is in `dedicatedMetadataFields`, with a row in TestRecordCASRefusesCritiqueOwnerWrite.

Production facts checked against the host, not only the fixtures:

- Real seat launch ids (`seat-<16 hex>`) match the launch store's idPattern, so `store.Read` returns
  not-found or a record, never ErrInvalidID.
- None of the 106 host seat records has an empty launchId; 105 of 106 carry reapedAt.
- The steward writes seat records atomically, with temp files named `*.tmp`, which the reader skips.
- No production code deletes seat records.
- All 28 goal-bound non-unit job records on the host are completed with an endedAt. No executed job would
  count open-ended to now.

Tests T2-T14 are present through ProjectBudget, ProjectBudgetWithoutRun, EvaluateGoalAdmission (bed.admission)
and ReserveUnitLaunch on real records. Every new bed asserts ElapsedLegacy false except the fallback tests. All new
tests and subtests are parallel. Extra beds cover all six S4 seat failures, window clipping (with a brief file and a
bad other-goal seat), and an undated live governed run. TC1 drives `work build` through the real unit runner. It
aligns only its own manager Store.Root with the `goal status` home, asserts a non-legacy known projection, and
prints the same non-zero `spent: elapsed` 14 hours apart. The fixture migration follows the classes; each changed
number is explained by D1/D6 (see observations 3-4). The builder's mutation table (e-s) names the failing test for
each mutation.

I ran the new and migrated dispatch tests locally and they pass. The frozen check is also green: LANDING-CHECKED 0,
the unit groups for dispatch/evidence/steward/launch/lease/proofrun/cmd green, and the audits ok.

## Checklist 2: the proof command

The proof command is `/usr/bin/true` and exercises nothing by itself. The evidence is the frozen unit check:
`metasystem test impact` plus the TestAudit suite, whole-package groups green, with TC1 and the migrated cmd beds
in the cmd selection. The new tests exercise the failure paths, not only the happy path:

- the undated job fallback and the undecodable seat fallback;
- the six seat faults: directory, record, startedAt, reapedAt, launch read and finishedAt;
- the undated live governed run;
- the required launch store, which stays unknown and refuses BUDGET_UNKNOWN rather than falling back;
- another goal's seat;
- clipping;
- the environment exclusion and its retry;
- a breach, from both admission and the live stop.

## Non-gating observations (not material)

1. RELATION: new. Scope, production seams outside the brief's named files: admission.go now passes
   `reads.BudgetHome` to ProjectBudget, and ReserveUnitLaunch takes a variadic `homes ...string`. Both are
   production-neutral. No production code sets goalAdmissionReads.BudgetHome, stop.go already passes it at three
   sites, and `ProjectBudget(..., "")` equals the no-home call. Every production ReserveUnitLaunch caller passes no
   home. The builder disclosed both; they only isolate test launch stores. Production lines: 163 against the
   110 estimate, under the 250 stop line, disclosed.
2. RELATION: new. Scope, internal/evidence/bound_test.go: the bed now appends "-case" to its checkout path until
   `diskstore.Segment` (12 hex digits of sha256) contains a letter. This is a fix for a flake that already
   existed in TestAnUpperCaseSpellingOfTheLiveSegmentIsNeverListed (about 0.36% of temp paths) and is unrelated
   to the clock. No assertion is weakened. realpath.Resolve resolves the longest existing prefix, so the
   precomputed segment matches the later one. The builder disclosed and listed it. A separate later-list item
   would have kept the unit pure.
3. RELATION: new. TestIdleCountsForAClaimNeverReleased starts its seat at 08:30. The brief's unclear-bed rule
   names "the seat starting at the latest claim", which is 08:00 and would read 2h. The test still pins that
   recorded idle seconds are not subtracted again, since that would read 60m, so the claim holds.
4. RELATION: new. The third row of TestIdleSecondsComeOffTheElapsedClockAfterTheDischargeStart now runs on an
   empty root, so the legacy path's `Elapsed < 0` clamp is reached only on fallback. No test now has idle seconds
   larger than wall time on that path. The own-work path cannot go negative.
5. RELATION: new. ownWorkElapsed treats a directory named `*.json` in the seat directory as an unreadable record
   and falls back to the legacy value; the steward's own reader skips directories. The same happens to a record
   removed between ReadDir and ReadFile. Nothing in production creates either case today, and the fallback is
   the safe direction.
6. RELATION: new. By design (S8), the migrated shared beds give equal numbers on the own-work and legacy paths and
   do not assert ElapsedLegacy. Only the new beds distinguish the two paths. This is as the brief specifies.

## Unchecked within the tool budget

Nothing on the checklist went unchecked. I did not rerun the builder's mutations or the whole cmd/metasystem
suite myself; I relied on the frozen check's green groups and the builder's mutation logs for those.

VERDICT: land
